   1 # DESIGN: Velvet Eclipse / 绯月赌城
   2 
   3 ## Visual Identity
   4 
   5 A moonlit gothic casino castle in rich illustrated, cel-shaded fantasy art. Indigo stone, burgundy curtains and aged-gold ornament surround a silver-violet-haired hunter; warm candles and luminous purple cards guide the eye toward the playable foreground.
   6 
   7 Sources: GDD.md §§4–7 and the eight inspected, user-supplied concepts identified in ASSETS.md. Their palette, character identity and architectural motifs guide original art; their pixel treatment, incidental lettering and extra systems do not expand the approved game.
   8 
   9 ## Image Style
  10 
  11 ### 1. Medium And Rendering
  12 
  13 Use expressive non-pixel illustration with clear character poses and ornate painted architecture.
  14 - Preserve illustrated shading and costume folds rather than reducing actors to geometric symbols.
  15 - Keep heroine, dealers, props and scenery within one coherent rendering family.
  16 - Do not claim exact pixel-art or one-to-one reproduction of the concepts.
  17 
  18 ### 2. Color And Value
  19 
  20 Dark indigo and wine-red surroundings make gold, candlelight and magic accents legible.
  21 - Use burgundy curtains, purple moonlight and fine aged-gold trim throughout the castle.
  22 - Reserve bright magenta/pink for readable card magic and selected emphasis.
  23 - Distinguish the spectral dealer with the references' cool cyan/green spectral treatment.
  24 
  25 ### 3. Shape And Silhouette
  26 
  27 Gothic arches and layered balconies frame identifiable, separated combat silhouettes.
  28 - Keep the heroine's short silver-violet hair, dark hunter outfit, flowing wine/violet accents and slender gold-accented sword recognizable.
  29 - Give skeletal dealers tall, readable silhouettes with role-specific equipment and spectral treatment.
  30 - Let the Royal Dealer dominate through a large regal skeletal silhouette without hiding the heroine.
  31 
  32 ### 4. Line And Edge
  33 
  34 Crisp actor contours and fine decorative edges distinguish the foreground from distant architecture.
  35 - Keep sword, hands, card corners and character outlines readable against dark stone.
  36 - Concentrate intricate linework in gold borders, carved fixtures and costume accents, as in the supplied concepts.
  37 - Do not simulate pixel art by quantizing or pixelating the illustration.
  38 
  39 ### 5. Material And Texture
  40 
  41 Stone, velvet, metal and spectral glow should read as different materials.
  42 - Give masonry carved depth, curtains visible folds and gold trim fine worn highlights.
  43 - Use warm wax-light accents around chandeliers, candles and the save shrine.
  44 - Keep magical cards and the ghost hand luminous rather than stone-like.
  45 
  46 ### 6. Lighting And Shadow
  47 
  48 Cool moonlight and warm candlelight coexist, with combat effects remaining distinct.
  49 - Use purple/blue ambient light behind warm local candle highlights.
  50 - Light platform tops clearly enough to identify landing surfaces.
  51 - Make boss phase two visibly change arena lighting without obscuring attacks or health information.
  52 
  53 ### 7. Space, Perspective, And Depth
  54 
  55 The game reads as side-on action layered over deep castle interiors.
  56 - Keep distant arches, windows and towers behind independent actors and foreground platforms.
  57 - Separate foreground rails, curtains and chandeliers into distinct depth layers.
  58 - No source concept may replace the assembled interactive room as a full-screen gameplay image.
  59 
  60 ### 8. Composition And Visual Hierarchy
  61 
  62 Heroine, threats, landing edges and the next usable interaction lead the composition.
  63 - Preserve clear space around the current combat and jump corridor.
  64 - Distinguish Lobby, Gallery and Save Room through foreground arrangement and lighting even when their distant plate is shared.
  65 - Keep prompts and HUD clear of important platform edges and attack warnings.
  66 
  67 ### 9. Detail Density And Abstraction
  68 
  69 Rich architectural detail supports a concise, readable playable layer.
  70 - Preserve casino identity through card suits, curtains, roulette imagery and gold ornament.
  71 - Simplify tiny decorative detail before sacrificing character pose or projectile clarity.
  72 - Treat chips as visual dressing; their presence must not imply an inventory or currency system.
  73 
  74 ## UI Visual Language
  75 
  76 Gold/purple frames and card-suit motifs carry the castle's visual identity into clear Chinese-first UI.
  77 - Use dark surfaces and restrained gold trim around important information.
  78 - Give health and card energy visually distinct bars with readable text, rather than color alone.
  79 - Keep Chinese labels prominent; the game title may be bilingual.
  80 - Use readable headings, short labels and separated controls; avoid the concepts' dense miniature text.
  81 - Differentiate selected, disabled and active controls visibly.
  82 - Make the discovered map, Moonstep badge, interaction prompts and save status truthful to current state.
  83 - Do not add portrait, inventory, shop or costume-selection panels from the reference montage.
  84 
  85 ## Do
  86 
  87 - Reuse the references' identifiable mood and motifs through original illustrated assets.
  88 - Preserve a genuine visual change when Moonstep is acquired and when the boss enters phase two.
  89 - Make damage, recovery, defeat and a safe checkpoint understandable through visuals.
  90 
  91 ## Don't
  92 
  93 - Substitute flat shapes, still actor cutouts or full-screen reference art for required illustrated assets and animation.
  94 - Bake gameplay actors, HUD, interactive relics or collision surfaces into distant backdrops.
  95 - Copy incidental reference branding, promise extra costumes, or imply gambling/payment functionality.
